task: You are given icrs_coords.csv with columns name,ra_deg,dec_deg for 3 stars in the ICRS (equatorial) frame. Using astropy.coordinates.SkyCoord, transform each coordinate to the Galactic frame and write galactic_coords.csv with columns name,l_deg,b_deg (one row per star, same order as the input).
verify:
import csv
expected = {
  'Star1': (121.1743, -21.5733),
  'Star2': (184.5575, -5.7844),
  'Star3': (309.4646, 19.4241),
}
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open('galactic_coords.csv')))
ok = len(rows) == 3
for r in rows:
    name = r['name']
    l, b = float(r['l_deg']), float(r['b_deg'])
    el, eb = expected.get(name, (None, None))
    ok = ok and el is not None and abs(l - el) < 0.05 and abs(b - eb) < 0.05
print(ok)
why: Frame transformations (ICRS->Galactic) require running astropy.coordinates code; there is no way to produce numerically correct output by writing a text file directly.

task: Two single-page PDF cover sheets, a.pdf and b.pdf, are in the current directory. Merge them into one file, merged.pdf, with a.pdf's page first followed by b.pdf's page, per the pdf skill's pypdf merge recipe.

inputs.generate_with_python:
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
c = canvas.Canvas('a.pdf', pagesize=letter)
c.drawString(100, 700, 'ALPHA-COVER-SHEET')
c.save()
c = canvas.Canvas('b.pdf', pagesize=letter)
c.drawString(100, 700, 'BETA-COVER-SHEET')
c.save()

verify:
from pypdf import PdfReader
r = PdfReader('merged.pdf')
ok = (len(r.pages) == 2 and 'ALPHA-COVER-SHEET' in r.pages[0].extract_text() and 'BETA-COVER-SHEET' in r.pages[1].extract_text())
print(ok)
why: A merged PDF is a binary file with its own object/xref structure; only running pypdf (or an equivalent library) can produce a valid one -- the Write tool can only emit text.

task: Create a spreadsheet workbook budget.xlsx with one sheet named 'Budget'. Row 1: A1='Item', B1='Cost'. Rows 2-4: item names and numeric costs -- Rent/1200, Utilities/150, Supplies/75 (A2:A4 the names, B2:B4 the numbers). Row 5: A5='Total', and B5 must be a live Excel formula (never a hardcoded number) that sums B2:B4, per the xlsx skill's 'formulas, never hardcoded results' rule.
verify:
from openpyxl import load_workbook
wb = load_workbook('budget.xlsx')
ws = wb['Budget']
formula = str(ws['B5'].value or '').strip().upper().replace(' ', '')
ok = (ws['A1'].value == 'Item' and ws['B1'].value == 'Cost' and
      ws['A2'].value == 'Rent' and float(ws['B2'].value) == 1200 and
      ws['A3'].value == 'Utilities' and float(ws['B3'].value) == 150 and
      ws['A4'].value == 'Supplies' and float(ws['B4'].value) == 75 and
      ws['A5'].value == 'Total' and formula == '=SUM(B2:B4)')
print(ok)
why: A .xlsx is a zip of XML parts; there is no way to hand-author a valid one as plain text -- producing it requires actually running openpyxl.

task: Create a Word document report.docx containing a Heading 1 paragraph with the exact text 'Quarterly Report', followed by a body paragraph with the exact sentence 'Revenue grew 12% year over year.'
verify:
from docx import Document
doc = Document('report.docx')
paras = doc.paragraphs
has_heading = any(p.style.name.startswith('Heading') and p.text.strip() == 'Quarterly Report' for p in paras)
has_body = any(p.text.strip() == 'Revenue grew 12% year over year.' for p in paras)
print(has_heading and has_body)
why: A .docx is a zip of XML parts (styles, document.xml, relationships); it can only be produced correctly by executing a library such as python-docx, not by writing text directly. (The skill's own suggested docx-js/npm route is not confirmed available in this sandbox; python-docx, which is preinstalled, accomplishes the same outcome.)
